solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Heavyweight jazzman finding time for right notes in this case

indicators.note: 'finding time' says a new letter is found to go into the name in a swap
'time for right' says that letter stands in place of the other one in the name

parts.note: Fats Waller, the famously large American jazz pianist

explanation.surface: A big jazz pianist chooses a different tempo for the correct notes in this piece.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface, 'notes' are musical and 'case' is an instance; the definition takes them as banknotes and a holder. Change the R in WALLER to T.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallet is the small folding holder in which banknotes are carried.

clue.text: This is the location of part of New York

definitions.text: This is the location of part of New York

parts.words: This is the location of part of New York
parts.note: names a Manhattan district, and this entry also sits on the left-hand edge of the grid

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is self-reference: 1-down runs along the grid's western edge, so 'This' (the entry) really is located on the west side.
explanation.definitionFit: West Side is the Manhattan district west of Fifth Avenue and Central Park.

clue.text: Disguise provenance of one coming ashore around mid-January

indicators.note: the lander's letters go around the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a lander is one who lands, coming ashore

indicators.note: mid-January takes the central letter of the seven-letter month

explanation.surface: A sailor landing in midwinter tries to hide where something came from.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder money is to pass it through legitimate channels so its criminal origin is hidden.

clue.text: Young singer on the up enthrals the old king

indicators.note: to enthral is literally to hold in thrall, so the reversed word holds the other inside it
in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a treble is a boy soprano

explanation.surface: A boy chorister rising in his career captivates an aged monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young singer' suggests a pop star, but here it is the boy's voice part in a choir; in a down clue 'on the up' reads it bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelbert was a king of Kent and later also a king of Wessex, both in the Anglo-Saxon era.

clue.text: Something appetising caught by grapple attached to pier

indicators.note: caught by says the answer is held within the joined words, so the outer letters around it are discarded
attached to says the two words are joined end to end before the answer is found inside them

parts.note: taken as written; its last five letters begin the answer
taken as written; its first three letters end the answer

explanation.surface: A tasty morsel is landed by a grappling hook fixed to a jetty.
explanation.walkthrough: Read gr|APPLE then PIE|r: 'attached to' tells you the two words are joined end to end, and the answer is caught across the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple pie is a classic baked dessert, certainly an appetising thing to eat.

clue.text: Badly exposed backs left QPR without cover

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put together in a wrong, jumbled order
exposed means stripped of its outer layer, so backs loses its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written; QPR is Queens Park Rangers, a London football club

explanation.surface: A football report: QPR's defenders were left exposed with nobody covering them.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip 'backs' to ACK, then shuffle ACK, L, QPR and WITHOUT together. The surface's 'without cover' reads as one phrase, but 'cover' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A patchwork quilt is a bedcover sewn from many small pieces of fabric.

clue.text: Clergyman raised under £1 for organ

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece written under another comes after it

parts.note: L stands for pound (from Latin libra) and I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word is lifted to read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar is lifted up for less than a pound to play the church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' looks musical next to a clergyman, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The liver is a large internal organ of the body that filters blood.

clue.text: Spooner's raunchy police movie provides fodder for Cineworld

indicators.note: Spooner's tells you to swap the opening sounds of two words, after William Spooner

parts.note: a cop is a police officer
porn, the explicit kind of film, is the raunchy sort; 'movie' then just completes the picture

explanation.surface: A smutty police film is shown at a big cinema chain.
explanation.walkthrough: COP PORN becomes POP CORN when the first letters are swapped. Cineworld is a UK cinema chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Popcorn is the snack eaten by audiences in cinemas, so food for moviegoers.

clue.text: What Schoenberg and Grieg do in a coda

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as three words
second meaning: a coda is the closing passage of a piece

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as END IN G and it describes the composers' names, which both finish with the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding section of a musical movement, the part that finishes it.

clue.text: Censors prod ten wayward journalists

indicators.note: wayward means going astray, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: Censors push ten unruly reporters into line.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondents are reporters who file news, often from abroad, for a paper or broadcaster.

clue.text: Young people avoiding Head being absorbed by golf, perhaps, here?

indicators.note: being absorbed by puts the trimmed word inside the other

parts.note: golf is an example of a sport

indicators.note: avoiding the head means the first letter is left off

parts.note: youth means young people collectively

explanation.surface: Teenagers skip a head teacher's lesson to play golf at a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' with a capital looks like a head teacher but only means the first letter. The definition is just 'here', made fair by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Southport, a Merseyside seaside town, is home to Royal Birkdale, a links course that hosts the Open.

clue.text: Flat where retired prima donna briefly stores a piano

indicators.note: stores means keeps inside, so the other letters go in
retired means withdrawn, going back, so the letters are read backwards
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a diva is a leading female opera singer, a prima donna
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: An apartment where a retired opera star keeps a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: DIVA cut short is DIV, which reversed gives VID; A and P go inside it. 'Flat' looks like a home, but it means dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapid means lacking liveliness or interest, dull in the way a flat performance is.

clue.text: One providing support not so happy about student

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes around the letter

parts.note: sadder means less happy
L is for learner, a student

explanation.surface: A counsellor who is less cheerful than usual takes on a student.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddler makes saddles, the leather seats that support a horse rider.

clue.text: No chat show host retracted something barbed

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Oprah Winfrey is the famous American chat show host

explanation.surface: A talk show presenter withdraws a cutting remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpoon is a spear with a barbed head, used for hunting whales and large fish.

clue.text: It's very slow with e-network going west

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west means read right to left, backwards

parts.note: E for electric, plus grid, the electricity network

explanation.surface: A complaint that an online network is sluggish as it fails.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a slow mournful song or lament, like music played at a funeral.

clue.text: Country place hosting races is short of a ground

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: Ascot is the Berkshire racecourse
land means ground

explanation.surface: A rural racecourse lacks a proper field.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT, the famous English racecourse, loses its A to give SCOT. 'Country place' reads together, but 'Country' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland is one of the four nations of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Hoped-for outcome for people tying love knots?

indicators.note: knots means tangles, so the letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: Couples who tie the knot hope their love lasts a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: Tying the knot means marrying, so 'tying love knots' looks like a phrase about weddings rather than an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Longevity means long life, which newlyweds hope their marriage enjoys.

clue.text: Pieces performed by old maids entertaining Ethel on vacation

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, holding the guest inside

parts.note: prudes are prim, easily shocked people, the old-maid stereotype

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, so the name loses all but its outer letters

explanation.surface: Elderly spinsters host their friend Ethel while performing music.
explanation.definitionFit: Preludes are short musical works, like those composed by Chopin, played as concert items.

clue.text: Foot's holding on to Labour saw cuts in production

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the first piece wraps around the next

parts.note: re means on, concerning
work means labour

explanation.surface: Labour leader Michael Foot clings to his party while cuts are seen in manufacturing.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot led Britain's Labour Party; the clue pretends to be about him. 'saw' reads as a past tense but is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretwork is ornamental openwork patterns made by cutting wood with a fine fretsaw.

clue.text: Elizabethan variety of hair gel

indicators.note: a variety of means a different version, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of styling product for hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was an explorer and courtier at the court of Queen Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Short cut … I'm not sure it's better

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a nick is a small cut
er is the hesitant noise of someone unsure

explanation.surface: Someone doubts whether a shorter haircut is an improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer is the comparative of nice, meaning more pleasant or agreeable.

clue.text: Promotion of cocaine in sale leads to formal warning

indicators.note: promotion means moving up, so the letter is moved to an earlier place in the word, at the top in a down entry

parts.note: an auction is a sale by bidding
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: Pushing cocaine in a sale earns a police caution.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the C of AUCTION up to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A caution is an official warning given by police instead of a prosecution.

clue.text: Female drivers' club introducing male joiner

indicators.note: introducing means bringing in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, Britain's motoring organisation
and is a conjunction, a word that joins

explanation.surface: A women's motoring club admits a man who is a carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' looks like a carpenter, but it is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amanda is a woman's given name, so it fits the label for a female.

clue.text: Liberal Democrat's plugging involved woman

indicators.note: plugging means filling a gap, so it goes inside the other word

parts.note: mired means entangled, involved in difficulty
LD is short for Liberal Democrat, a British party

explanation.surface: A Lib Dem politician is promoting a woman she is involved with.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildred is a woman's given name, so it fits the label for a female person.

clue.text: Device setting pulses racing monitors those on the rebound

definitions.text: Device setting pulses racing monitors those on the rebound

parts.words: Device setting pulses racing monitors those on the rebound
parts.note: describes the detection system: it sends out radio pulses and tracks their echoes as they bounce back; the word itself reads the same either way

explanation.walkthrough: 'setting pulses racing' sounds like excitement and 'on the rebound' like heartbreak; read literally they describe signals sent out and bouncing back.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar detects objects by emitting radio waves and measuring the reflections that return.

clue.text: 50% of equity seized by a Spanish lawcourt at the outset? That's unfair

indicators.note: seized by means held inside, so the half-word goes inside

parts.note: una is Spanish for a (feminine)
the first half of the six-letter word equity

indicators.note: at the outset picks the first letter of lawcourt

explanation.surface: A Spanish court seizes half a company's shares at the start, which seems unjust.
explanation.definitionFit: Unequal treatment is uneven or biased, so unequal can mean not just or not even-handed.

clue.text: Scotsman returns bill for classical water feature

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name
an ad is an advertisement, a bill posted up

explanation.surface: A Scot sends back the invoice for an old-style fountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water feature' sounds like a garden fountain but means a figure from classical myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a nymph of Greek mythology who lives in rivers, springs or lakes.

clue.text: I'll find EU in disarray — or abolished?

indicators.note: in disarray means in a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Brexit-era quip: will I find the EU in chaos, or gone altogether?
explanation.definitionFit: Nullified means cancelled or made void, as a law that has been abolished.

clue.text: Gnome beginning to snort morphia is high

indicators.note: being high on a drug leaves one disordered, so the letters are scrambled
beginning to picks the first letter of snort

explanation.surface: A garden gnome takes drugs and gets stoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnome' looks like a garden ornament, but a gnome is also a pithy saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome in this sense is a short maxim, the same as a pithy saying or adage.

clue.text: Extremely hardy eutherian Africans

indicators.note: extremely picks the extreme letters, first and last, of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A description of tough placental mammals native to Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Eutherian means placental mammal; the whole clue both builds the answer and describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyenas are tough African scavenging carnivores, and like all placental mammals they are eutherians.
